Question: What made White people so powerful and dominant on the global stage?
Answer: Seafaring. For whatever reason, the Europeans were much more interested in seafaring than any of the other large cultures. Other countries had great ships, but they didn't explore the world, looking for trade goods the way Europeans did. Large ships armed with cannons allowed them to dominate cultures without cannons. This allowed the Spanish to conquer Mexico and much of South America. The Portuguese got Brazil. These were relatively little countries that became very rich stealing the resources from the Americas. Once the USA separated from the UK, they did the same thing. The French and British tread a little softer in the Americas, but gun boat diplomacy gained them incredible riches in Asia. When you are pillaging gold, precious gems, spices, and antiquities from ancient cultures, it makes you very rich, and you can afford the best navies. Which makes you more powerful. Once they had the money, they could afford efficient government and policing. This lowers corruption and makes them richer. So the white people got a head start, because of their seafaring. They boomed, and now the rest of the world is catching up. Unfortunately climate change, might put a crimp in this.

Question: Is it bad to not welcome uninvited guests to your party?
Answer: I have always welcomed uninvited guests, I am on good terms with just about everyone I know. It was common growing up, that people would just stop by, our house was like a second home. My brother on the other hand, does not want uninvited guests. I remember when he moved into his first house, my parents showed up with a house warming gift, unannounced. He refused to let them in. My parents quickly learned what his house rules were, and obeyed them. It was a shock to them, as no one in our community refused to allow in uninvited guests. But they recognized my brothers right to set his own house rules. If you are having a party, it would depend on the party. A formal sit down dinner party, with exactly enough Cornish game hens, and desserts to go around, is the only situation where I might not welcome an uninvited guest. The more the merrier to a costume party, or a new years eve party.

Question: What are some common places people go to when they need a break from everything?
Answer: Some people go to bars and clubs to let off steam and unwind. It was one of my favorite ways to take a break. Going and sitting in the trees on the riverbank, and watching nature was also a good way to unwind. Studies have shown that your blood pressure drops when surrounded by green trees. Dropping a line in the water and dreaming of catching a fish, just completed the experience. I also did extreme things. When I was snowmobiling, all my attention had to be on snowmobiling. One wrong move, and you can drop into a crevasse, hit a tree, fall through the ice, etc. The same was true for scuba diving, especially cave and wreck diving, you can't think about anything else, and expect to survive consistently. The same was true for hang gliding, racing around the track, snowboarding and white water rafting. To a lesser extent it's true of water skiing, canoeing on a river, cliff diving, and atving. That's what I did when I needed a break, I don't go to the bar very often anymore.

Question: I bought a house and found stock certificates. The person is deceased whos name is on them. Can I do anything with them?
Answer: When my uncle died, he had a safety deposit box full of paper stock certificates. I immediately thought I was rich, and I took them to my broker, who said he hated checking these things out, but he did, and they were worthless. So, if you have a stock broker, send him a picture, and ask him to check them out, maybe you will be luckier than me.

Question: Do doctors in emergency rooms or departments ever tell patients they shouldn't have come to the emergency room with something so minor?
Answer: The triage nurse kicked a guy out of emergency, while I was waiting for my wife. He had come in looking for a covid vaccination. He wanted to fly somewhere, and at the time, airlines weren't allowing the unvaccinated to fly. You could then go online and show that you were vaccinated. All of the pharmacies gave vaccinations, and some of the doctors offices, but it was after closing. Evidently when he went to online check in, it required proof of vaccination. He wanted the vaccination immediately, so he could fly that night. The triage nurse, said that it wasn't an emergency, he had weeks to get his shot, and told him to leave. The online website was only updated once a day, so he still wouldn't have had proof, even if he was vaccinated.

Question: Do the people in Canada know that the Green Party or the People’s Party exist as an alternative to liberal and conservative governments? It seems like all you hear about is Liberal and Conservative.

When the Green party said that it supported vaccine mandates, instead of the natural way of doing things, its numbers plunged in the polls, by the exact same numbers, that the People's partys rose, after they said that they opposed mandated vaccinations. When NDP candidates in Atlantic Canada left the party, because they said that they couldn't get elected if their leader wore a turban, they were welcomed by the Green party. The Green party doesn't have a stance on many of the political hot button issues, so it doesn't make the papers.

Question: Is it possible to eliminate unelected senators and have a directly elected House of Commons in Canada?
Answer: We already have a directly elected House of Commons in Canada. To remove the senate would be a huge undertaking, with major constitutional changes. This would require support from provinces that benefit from the current senate. So this is highly unlikely to happen. So having an elected senate is the next best thing, but this would also require a somewhat smaller, but still huge change to the constitution. Harper attempted a get around, to all of this. He wanted all the provinces to elect a pool of senators in waiting. To run for the election, you would have to sign a contract that you would resign eight or ten years after being appointed to the senate. This effectively sets a term limit. Then he would pass a law that the PM must only appoint people from each provinces senator pool. This gave us an elected senate with term limits. Alberta has been electing senators for 40 years and Trudeau is the first PM to refuse to appoint an elected senator. This would have largely gotten around the constitutional issues. But Ontario's premier Wynne refused to cooperate, so Harper lost what he considered to be his biggest legacy. He had a hissy fit and refused to meet with her for three years. This methodology is the only way we have a hope of getting an elected senate.
